entities.summary:
Aeroflot — Russian Airlines is the flag carrier of Russia, founded in 1923 as the world's oldest national airline still in continuous operation. Once the world's largest airline in Soviet times, Aeroflot served as the state aviation monopoly connecting the USSR's vast territory and projecting Soviet power internationally.

In Soviet times, Aeroflot was more than an airline — it was a government ministry operating over 100 aircraft types, employing over 400,000 workers, and maintaining routes to every corner of the USSR's 11 time zones. Its size was extraordinary: in 1976 it carried over 100 million passengers, more than any airline in history at that time. Soviet Aeroflot also functioned as a troop transport and cargo system serving military and government needs.

Post-Soviet Aeroflot shed its regional subsidiaries as Russia's republics formed independent airlines, focusing on international routes from Sheremetyevo Moscow. Its safety record, once abysmal, improved dramatically with fleet modernization using Western Airbus and Boeing aircraft. Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine triggered sweeping Western sanctions grounding 500+ aircraft leased from Western lessors, stranding Russia's aviation industry and forcing Aeroflot to rely on domestic Sukhoi Superjet and older aircraft while Western parts dwindled.
